title: Appliance Rebates in Windsor 2026: Up to $200 Per Appliance
desc: Windsor appliance rebates for 2026: $25 to $200 from Home Renovation Savings, with Enwin Utilities as distributor.
lead: Windsor has 94,275 households and one of the mildest Januaries on our list, -6.2°C. Six appliance rebates run from $25 to $200.
cards_heading: What Ontario pays for new appliances in Windsor
cards_intro: We re-read the program's appliance page on October 4, 2026. The rebates are province-wide, so the amounts are the same in every city, and the rules about what you replace and which model you buy are what decide a claim.

cards.title: Heat pump clothes dryer
cards.note: The largest of the six appliance rebates, for a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient heat pump dryer replacing an electric dryer.

cards.title: Induction cooktop or range
cards.note: For a new induction cooktop or range on the program's product list, replacing an existing electric one.

cards.title: Washing machine
cards.note: For a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient washer on the program list.

cards.title: Fridge
cards.note: For a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient refrigerator replacing an existing electric one.

cards.title: Freezer
cards.note: For a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient freezer on the list.

cards.title: Dishwasher
cards.note: For a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient dishwasher on the list.

cards.title: Who can claim
cards.note: A residential customer on the Ontario grid with an existing electric appliance in need of replacing. Cornwall Electric customers are excluded.

cards.title: Free route
cards.note: Income-qualified households can get energy-efficient fridges and freezers at no charge, along with other upgrades.

after_cards: The appliance page states no end date, so confirm it is still open before you buy.
sections: 63% of Windsor households own and 37% rent, with 60% in detached houses. The page does not say owners only, and a tenant should clear a swap with the landlord.
Enwin Utilities supplies electricity and Windsor postal codes begin with N, which the Energy Affordability Program lists for free fridges and freezers under its income limits.

The six rebates are $200 for a heat pump dryer, $150 for an induction cooktop or range, $75 for a washer, $50 each for a fridge and a freezer and $25 for a dishwasher. A household that replaced all six would receive $550, though few Windsor homes will need to swap everything at once. The rebate is flat, so it takes the same amount off an entry model and a premium one.

The program page asks for an existing electric appliance in need of replacing. A new fridge to go in a spare corner, or an induction range where the kitchen had no range, is not a replacement. If you are switching from gas to an electric appliance, the page does not say whether that counts, so ask the program before you buy. Windsor households that already cook on an electric range are the clearest fit for the induction rebate.

About 68% of Windsor's 94,275 households live in homes built before 1981. Age of the house tells you little about the age of the fridge, and a working appliance rarely pays back a swap through a $25 to $200 rebate alone. The rebate suits a replacement you already need to make.
Most Efficient, not just ENERGY STAR

The rebate is for ENERGY STAR Most Efficient models, which the page describes as going beyond standard ENERGY STAR requirements. A fridge with the ordinary ENERGY STAR mark may not qualify. Each appliance has its own product list linked from the program page, so find the model number there before you pay, whether you buy in Windsor or online.
claim_steps: Check that the appliance you are replacing is electric and that you are on the Ontario grid.
Find a new model on the program's ENERGY STAR Most Efficient list for that appliance.
Buy it new from any retailer and keep the receipt.
Upload the receipt on the program page within 60 days of purchase.
If your household income is under the limits, call 1-844-770-3148 about free fridges and freezers first.
